_why: #18, measured live 2026-09-08. `SKILL.md` §"Drive the gate through `h_mad_audit_cycle.py`" instructs passing `--gated`/`--legs`/`--project-tests`/`--suite-cmd` on the DRIVER, and `_cmd_audit_cycle` — the only supported entry point — rejected all four at `_unknown_opt` and forwarded none. Seven cycles across three document types on one feature emitted `AUDITCYCLE:` alone, and `audit_cycles` read `{plan:0, design:0, impl_plan:0}` after all of them, so `--round-cap` and `--exit-check` had nothing to count at the exact moment the two-round cap was supposed to bind. Five gates shipped, fully tested, and unreachable from the path that runs. Each row restores one half of that: the flag is refused, or it is accepted and quietly dropped.

mutations.name: the-wrapper-rejects-gated-again
mutations._mechanism: `--gated` falls through to `_unknown_opt`, so no cycle can ever write a gate stamp. `audit_cycles` stays at 0 forever and `--round-cap`/`--exit-check` remain uncomputable — the precise state measured across seven live cycles.

mutations.name: the-wrapper-rejects-project-tests-again
mutations._mechanism: No `SUITE:` line, so a red project suite cannot block an exit. The suite gate (#91) shipped and becomes unreachable.

mutations.name: gated-is-parsed-and-then-dropped
mutations._mechanism: The nastier half: the option loop ACCEPTS `--gated`, so nothing errors and the caller believes the gate ran, while the driver never receives it. Acceptance is not forwarding, and a silently-dropped flag is worse than a rejected one because the rejection at least tells you.
mutations.find: for g in ${gated[@]+"${gated[@]}"}; do helper_args+=(--gated "$g"); done

mutations.name: legs-is-parsed-and-then-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Same shape for the leg set. `GATE-LEGS:` never renders, so a phase can exit on an incomplete leg set with nothing recording which surfaces ran — exactly the H3 case observed live, where a design phase exited on one surface and the owed codex leg later returned 12 musts and reopened it.
mutations.find: for l in ${legs[@]+"${legs[@]}"};  do helper_args+=(--legs  "$l"); done

mutations.name: the-option-loop-swallows-everything
mutations._mechanism: The inverse direction, and it needs its own row because every other mutation here restores a REJECTION. If `_unknown_opt` stopped firing, a typo like `--getd` would be accepted in silence and the gate would go unrun with no error at all — the same failure wearing a friendlier face.
